validation.contextAndScope: Full CXL RAS/poison troubleshooting article; focus was state-changing Clear Poison semantics, ndctl poison-list source/offset interpretation, and a universal device-replacement threshold.
validation.signalAndRefutation: The article showed clear-media-poison as a routine remove command and did not warn that clear does not restore data. Linux implementation sends a 64-byte zero write-data payload. Restricting the command to confirmed test-injected poison and warning about data recovery/device policy refutes routine operational use.
validation.causeAndAlternatives: The command name invites interpreting it as metadata-only cleanup; actual device behavior is protocol/vendor dependent. Poison list disappearance can mean state cleared without restoring affected contents; collect backup/recovery and vendor platform guidance before any production action.
validation.evidence: Compared ndctl cxl list documentation (DPA/source fields and supported options) with Linux drivers/cxl/core/memdev.c Clear Poison payload, core/trace.h event fields, and pci.c event handling. Removed universal replacement threshold and linked the official sources in the article.
validation.sampleScope: Full article prose and all named command/trace examples were reviewed against official docs/source. No cxl command, device, host, poison injection, or event path was executed.
validation.decision: Remediated: require first listing the target DPA/source, limit clear to test-injected poison, state that Linux sends zero write-data and that clear is not data recovery, and use trends with vendor service criteria rather than a universal replacement threshold.
validation.smallestSafeChangeAndRollback: Changed the affected command framing, added a data-loss/recovery warning and four source links, and qualified the replacement decision. Preserve slug/date/draft/seriesOrder; rollback boundary is this article file.
validation.verificationAndResidualRisk: Per-file publish gate, inline-math and diff checks pass. Upstream cited-symbol check is SKIPPED because the Linux source clone is absent (not PASS). Hardware and version-specific ndctl/kernel/device behavior remain untested.
